subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a songbird perched on a branch, styled with Bauhaus geometric shapes and primary colors, needing a full skeleton with named joints and a separable upper and lower beak in rest pose. I want to keep the implementation careful and correct against the SDK while staying within a manageable length.

For composition, I'm thinking blue egg-shaped body, white belly, red striped wings, black-and-yellow triangle tail, yellow head with concentric circle eyes, and red triangular beak cones, perched on a dark wooden branch decorated with geometric leaves and berries. I'm working out real-world proportions—a robin-sized bird around 14-15cm with a 0.4m branch—and making sure the branch sits at floor level so the bird's feet rest properly above it at y=0.024.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a root hips joint, a spine chain built from catmull-rom points running from tail to chest, and a neck chain extending up from the spine to where the head will attach.

Still defining joints...

For wings I'm reconsidering the rest pose—rather than folded tight, I'll angle them outward slightly to match an "extended and separated" stance, and I'm thinking of modeling each wing as a flat extruded leaf-like shape rather than a simple tube sweep, which means figuring out orientation vectors along the chain.

Working out wing orientation vectors...

Now I'm shaping the wing as a quarter-disc outline, trying an elliptical arc with center at the shoulder and radii roughly 0.095 by 0.055 to give it a Bauhaus-style curved silhouette rather than a sharp triangular shape.

Working out the layered stripe effect now — stacking scaled quarter discs in red, yellow, and blue to get a Bauhaus feel, then figuring out the outward thickness axis for each covert layer using a cross-product against the vertical axis.

Placing the wing at the shoulder offset and checking it meets the body surface at the right radius, then starting to sketch the body as a swept sphere shape along the spine path.

Defining spine and neck joint chains...

Continuing the spine path upward to mid, chest, neck, and head points, placing the head sphere forward and up so total bird height from branch to crown comes to around 0.166m. Now I'm planning the tail as a fan shape extending back and down from the rear point, made of a short chain of segments tapering outward.

Working out the tail's trapezoid cross-section and orientation, tilting the tail downward with a slight slope and computing the perpendicular thickness direction so the flat shape stays properly oriented.

For the tail itself, I'm deciding on a simple Bauhaus-style fan of three triangular feathers at slight angles (around -12°, 0°, +12°), picking a color palette like red, yellow, and blue, and now choosing the body's blue tone.

I'm now working out the rest of the bird's anatomy: yellow sphere head, a decal-style eye (white disc, black ring, red pupil) on each side, and a two-part cone beak -- red on top, black on the bottom. For the belly, I'm considering a cream-colored sector blended into the body sweep for a softer underside.

For the chest, I like the idea of a Bauhaus-style decal -- a bold red circle emblem with a smaller concentric yellow circle layered on top, positioned slightly forward and down on the body. I'm figuring out how the cream belly sector and the chest emblem's placement interact so they read cleanly together.

I'm also planning out the texture budget overall -- aiming for 5-12 total, covering the eye (concentric SVG), the chest emblem, maybe a leaf/triangle pattern, cheek details, and a painted grain texture for the branch to keep that Bauhaus geometric-but-natural feel.

For the branch itself, I'm thinking dark brown grain with cut-end discs in cream or red as accent caps, while the leaves become pure Bauhaus shapes -- triangles, flat-cylinder circles, and squares in primary colors mounted on little twig stems. For the legs, I'm sketching thin black rod tarsi running from body to branch, with toes arranged three forward and one back.

Now I'm working out the leg joint kinematics, placing the hip and foot targets and figuring out bend directions so the ankle flexes backward slightly like a real bird's leg, keeping the tarsus simple as a two-bone limb anchored just below the body's radius.

Mapping out the toe geometry now, with three front toes and one back toe modeled as thin rods curving from the foot tip down around the branch surface.

I realize each toe should just be a single rod from the foot joint to the tip, but the geometry is tricky since the branch curves away — toes placed straight would stick out past the branch surface instead of wrapping around it. I'm considering thickening the branch radius slightly so the toes can realistically curl around it like a real bird's grip.

Working out exact coordinates for the branch radius, toe thickness, and foot height so the toes sit flush on top and curl down around the branch surface...

Settling on mid toe point with distance 0.0172 and tip point at 0.0163, both within the gripping radius. I'm mirroring the hind toe with a sideways angle, and now working out the branch sweep geometry with wavy catmull points and circumscribed radius constraints so it stays touching the ground at y=0.

Checking that the branch surface lines up under the bird's feet at those x-positions, verifying the catmull-rom curve passes close enough to the target y-value near the perch point.

Thinking about how to attach the branch prop in the rig—if parts auto-bind to the nearest joint, the branch could get wrongly attached to the foot and move with it, so I should explicitly bind all branch parts to the root hips bone to keep it static rather than creating a second root joint, which isn't allowed.

I need a shape helper for colors and textures now. I'm designing the eye as a Bauhaus-style decal with concentric circles in black, white, and blue plus a small highlight square, then placing it on the head sphere surface facing forward-side.

Getting the eye hit point with a non-null assertion, then designing the chest emblem as a red disc with a cream triangle and small black circle, and sketching a Bauhaus-style head split using a paint rule based on a y-coordinate threshold for the crown color.

I want to try a diagonal split instead, combining y and z coordinates into a plane equation so the black cap cuts diagonally across the head, then checking that the eye position still lands safely in the yellow zone given that line.

For wings and tail, I'm considering whether to keep them flat-colored quarter-discs or add textured decals like feather stripes, leaf veins, or an emblem card to give more visual richness beyond flat Bauhaus color blocks.

Leaves could be simple extrudes split diagonally into two colors for that half-red-half-yellow Bauhaus look, and wings might get concentric quarter-disc stripes plus a row of small cylinder dots for pattern — I need to figure out which wing face is outward-facing so the dots sit correctly on the surface.

Still computing dot placement...

Working out the wing attachment geometry...

I need to check that the wing base hugs the body surface correctly, since at the shoulder point the body radius is wider than the wing's inset offset, so the wing partially embeds into the body which should look fine, but I should verify this stays consistent as the body narrows further down the side.

For the wing's joint chain, I'm setting up shoulder, elbow, and wrist points along the top edge, with three joints naming the chain so it has a proper tip, and parenting it to the chest joint in the spine. I'll keep the wing layers rigged to the shoulder joint rather than splitting across elbow/wrist since fine articulation isn't essential here.

Now moving to the head and beak: the head sphere gets a radius around 0.027, and I'm building the upper beak as a four-sided cone (pyramid-style) in red, with a small base radius and length, positioned forward off the head's front point using a direction vector so it angles correctly.

For the lower beak, I'm adding a smaller black cone sitting on the jaw bone, slightly below and offset from the upper beak's axis, aimed forward from a jaw joint position relative to the head center.

Working out the beak geometry relative to the head sphere, sinking the base slightly so it blends in, and checking overall bird proportions against a typical songbird's length—settling on a slightly oversized stylized beak. Now moving on to the neck joint chain connecting to the head bone, and starting to think about the crest.

For the crest I'm imagining a Bauhaus-style design: a sharp, swept-back triangle extruded with thickness, oriented so it stands upright on top of the head, leaning forward slightly like a cockatoo's crest, positioned just above and in front of the head's center.

For the cheeks I'm considering a simple blue disc decal, and relying on the eye texture itself to provide a white ring highlight rather than adding separate geometry.

For the tail I'm planning a fan arrangement of three plates attached at the tail joints, rigidly following the tail bone chain.

Still defining plate geometry...

I'm offsetting the side plates slightly below the center plate to avoid z-fighting at the root. For the tail, I'm laying out a chain of points with a gradual downward slope and tapering height, then considering how to bind the plates to the tail bones so they move correctly when joints rotate.

Still working out the body bone hierarchy -- spine chain parented to hips, with joint positions slightly offset from the parent root. For the body sweep, I'm defining the path and radii with bone bindings and color sectors, and thinking through whether to build the path using a catmull spline for smoother curvature.

I'm computing radii at each point along the body, factoring in arc-length spacing between joints so the taper feels proportional rather than evenly distributed by index.

Adjusting the width profile values...

Now I'm checking the bone chaining for the sweep — spine chain ends where neck chain begins, sharing the junction joint so the skin stays continuous, with spine producing two joints and neck two more, and head's joint parenting off the last neck joint.

I'm placing the head joint at the neck's endpoint, slightly offset forward to align with the head sphere. For the tail and legs, I'm parenting them off hips and spine joints, and I still need to add a decal for the chest marking using a surface normal lookup around the body's front.

Now I'm thinking about adding color variation to the body, like a yellow rump patch defined by a band threshold on the t-parameter, with the rest using the base color.

So bands end at 0.2 yellow then 1 blue, finishing that structure. Now I'm working out the wing covering as concentric quarter-disc layers centered at the shoulder, with red, yellow, and blue scaled rings stacked outward with small offsets and thin black dots accenting the top layer.

Building the quarter-disc outline with 8 arc steps, checking it's convex and non-self-intersecting, then extruding it into a hanging shape along the negative y-axis. I'm also planning eye decals on the head and considering whether to add a small brow detail for a Bauhaus-style look.

Now I'm designing a `leaf` helper for branch decor: extruding equilateral triangle outlines, deciding how to orient the leaf plates in 3D (facing front/back with thickness along z), and figuring out how to rotate the 2D outline to vary twig angles.

Still defining twig geometry...

I'll angle the end disc slightly along the tangent direction and add a smaller red disc offset on top for a decorative ring effect. I'll skip extra details like nostrils, eyebrows, and toe claws, keeping the chest emblem as the main decoration, and decide against adding a cheek circle or collar decal to avoid overcomplicating the design.

Instead I'm considering a third decal for the back—a zigzag row of alternating triangles in red, yellow, and black placed along the top of the body as a saddle-like stripe pattern.

I'm figuring out the ray origin for the top of the body, then checking which imports from the builder library I actually need so I don't trip unused-locals errors during typecheck.

Defining color palette and wood grain texture...

Now I'm sketching the skeleton structure, starting with the builder setup and root hip joint, then laying out the body's spine points from hips up to the neck.

Checking the head placement against the chest radius to confirm the head and body spheres overlap enough to merge into one chunky, rounded bird silhouette rather than looking disconnected. Still writing the chain hierarchy...

Now working on the legs: mirroring left/right using a sign variable, setting hip and foot joint positions, and defining the bent limb chain with its segment lengths and bend direction so the leg geometry resolves correctly.

I'm also weighing color choices for the legs and toes against the dark wood body—considering black versus red to either echo the red beak and wing or stay subdued, and whether the wood should be lightened to make black legs read clearly.

Now I'm working out the leg sweep geometry, anchoring it near the base of the body, then figuring out how to derive the foot tip joint and build toe joints branching off the foot toward each digit's endpoint.

Writing toe path arrays...

Now I'm setting up the wing joint chain, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the spine, with the chain positioned symmetrically by side offset and tapering toward the wingtip.

Now I'm working out the extrusion parameters for the shoulder shape, figuring out the outward offset direction based on the tilt so the thickness pushes away from the body rather than into it, computing the orthogonal basis vectors for the s=1 case.

Then I'm checking the s=-1 mirrored case to confirm the outward offset points the opposite way as expected, and sketching out how to place the decorative dots on the wing using cylinder geometry positioned on a ring at roughly 0.86 average radius.

Now I'm thinking about adding a few black accent dots over the red ring, and reconsidering whether the wing should read as "folded" in the overall silhouette, plus adding a small Bauhaus-style circle detail.

Writing crest geometry code...

I'm checking that the crest sits embedded properly within the head sphere's geometry, confirming the peak height and verifying the base position is correctly nested under the surface. Then I'm adding a black cap region to the head using a paint function that splits color by position, with the red crest triangle emerging through it.

I'm using faceted shading on the low-poly head sphere for a clean low-poly look, then placing eye decals by azimuth and elevation around the head's surface, checking the chord length at that angle to size and position the eyes correctly on the front sides.

Adjusting the elevation slightly downward so the eye doesn't overlap into the black cap region, and confirming the eye's black-ring-then-white-disc structure makes exact positioning less critical since the ring blends into dark areas anyway. Now moving on to sizing the chest emblem decal.

I'm designing the emblem as concentric circles -- black outer ring, cream inset, red disc, and a yellow triangle with a small black center dot -- to create a layered badge look on the belly. For the saddle texture, I'm sketching a stacked triangle pattern within a tall narrow viewbox.

Still writing triangle decals...

I'm restricting the cream sector to start partway down so the rump stays yellow underneath, keeping sectors non-overlapping per spec, and figuring the cream belly region should blend naturally up toward the throat since the head sphere covers the transition anyway.

Now I'm working out the tail plate geometry—placing a root offset behind the body, defining side plates as small triangles angled outward in red, and a larger center plate outline with a paint region, layering them with slight y-offsets for thickness.

Checking proportions though: measuring beak to tail gives roughly 0.27m total body length, which is too long for a typical songbird (0.15-0.2m), so I'm scaling the tail down—shrinking the center plate to about 0.1 and side plates to 0.08 to keep things realistic.

Now I'm working out the tail chain geometry and its rotation around the Y axis, figuring out how the base direction vector and the rotated x-axis relate so the tail bends naturally from its root segment.

Writing leaf outline generator...

Working out leaf placement on each twig, extruding leaf shapes oriented along the branch with specific offsets, sizes, and rotations so they vary naturally along the twig tips.

Checking that nothing dips below the ground and leaves don't block the bird, then I'm setting up the branch as a bone joint attached at the hips with wavy sweep geometry and wood coloring, using octagonal cross-sections with flat bottom faces sitting exactly at the radius.

Skipping extra decorative rings in favor of simple cylinder cap discs, with the bird's weight centered at x=0 and feet offset slightly outward on the branch. Now I'm writing a helper function to build cone-shaped parts between two joints, computing direction and length from the base to tip points.

Working out beak geometry next, placing the upper beak cone near the head center with a slightly tilted base and tip, and starting the lower beak cone below it with similar low-poly coordinates.

I'm now thinking about the jaw joint hinge, keeping the beak as separate upper and lower parts, and whether to pose the jaw slightly open (around 8 degrees) for a more natural, readable look, making sure parts built after the pose still inherit it correctly.

Deciding against extra details like eyebrow bars or collar rings, keeping the design minimal with just the existing eye surround and wing bars. I'm confirming the body curve uses the catmull spline positions correctly, and double-checking the vector math for the chain segments.

Now I'm working out the leg using an inverse-kinematics limb function, passing hip and foot positions with segment lengths and bend directions, then sweeping a tube along the resulting joint chain for the leg geometry. I'm verifying the leg segment lengths add up correctly to span from hip to foot.

Verifying the body-leg geometry checks out, I move on to writing the module code, starting with the imports from the agentic-3js-builder library and confirming the Joint type is properly exported.

Writing bird construction code...

Still defining joints and wing geometry...

Adding layered color rings and dot details...

Now checking the wing geometry against the body silhouette, making sure the wing's lower edge and shoulder placement align properly with the body surface so nothing overlaps or floats awkwardly near the chest and leg areas.

That's a 2cm gap below the body, which might pass as a loosely folded wing, but I'm questioning the quarter-disc orientation itself—maybe I should flip it so the straight edges run along the top and front while the rounded edge sweeps from front to back-bottom, with the leading edge up and the tip trailing toward the back.

Instead I'm trying a different approach: tilting the wing's direction vectors so it slopes downward and back, giving it a more bird-like silhouette with the tip lower and further back, while keeping the front edge hanging slightly below the body. I'm recalculating the wing's position and radii against the body's surface curvature to make sure the leading corner sits just outside the chest.

Computing the leading edge endpoint and dot placements along the arc, then moving on to writing the actual TypeScript code for the wing vector calculations.

Defining wing joint positions and a rotation helper for leaf outline shapes, then laying out different leaf polygon types like triangles and squares for variation.

Now I'm setting up the twig sweeps with bone attachments and wood coloring, checking that twig thickness starts correctly at the branch surface, and wiring up the head joint and decal calls.

For the eye decal, I'm placing it at the hit point using the Frame-based PointInput. For the chest emblem, I'm positioning it using `around` with an elevation angle so it lands on the lower-front chest region, making sure it doesn't overlap the head.

For the saddle, I'm casting a ray down the back to find the surface hit, then placing the decal there using the hit's normal for orientation. For the branch end caps, I'm computing a small flat disc geometry positioned at the path's start point, aligning its direction with the tangent of the curve at that end.

Now I'm working through the right end cap similarly, orienting it along the upward-sloping tangent there, then layering a smaller red cylinder inside the larger cream one to create a protruding effect at the flat cap. For the tail, I'm chaining four catmull points into three joint segments and planning plate placements offset from the root joint along the bone.
